supersessionReason: Independent acceptance review found that v6 did not define fail-closed behavior when an already-published latest pointer later fails exact-byte verification, prevent an older not-modified confirmation from reviving it, or define recovery when a publication event commits before its pointer while a concurrent newer failure advances the heartbeat clock.

postPublicationCorruption.event: append one deterministic corrupt_object failure event and alert
postPublicationCorruption.heartbeat: transition to a non-current status and retain the immutable last-known pointer for auditability
postPublicationCorruption.pointerRule: an unchanged pointer may remain after permanent ineligibility only when the update is non-current, does not advance last success, and does not change source, provider, or dataset identity
postPublicationCorruption.selectionRule: a permanently ineligible capture may never be selected as a new pointer or transition back to current
postPublicationCorruption.notModifiedRule: a not-modified confirmation must exclude permanently ineligible heads and may clear a failure only when it is not older than the latest attempt

publicationRetryRecovery.precondition: the deterministic publication event and a pointer-publication failure event for the same capture both exist
publicationRetryRecovery.orderingRule: retry publishes only when the candidate is the deterministic eligible head; it returns without mutation only when the retained pointer is the same capture or is deterministically newer
publicationRetryRecovery.concurrentFailureRule: a newer unrelated heartbeat failure clock cannot strand an otherwise deterministic eligible head
publicationRetryRecovery.unknownOutcomeRule: a prior publication event without a matching pointer-publication failure and without its pointer is an inconsistent outcome that fails closed
publicationRetryRecovery.postconditionRule: when the deterministic pointer is installed but a causally newer attempt has already made the heartbeat non-current, publication succeeded and must not overwrite, relabel, or heal that newer failure
publicationRetryRecovery.failureJournalRule: journal pointer-publication failure only when the required pointer or current state is absent and no causally newer attempt explains the postcondition

effectiveContract: source-capture-contract.2026.1 plus v2, v3 except its superseded same-batch pointer clause, v4 except its superseded manifest-time verification clause, v5, v6, and every clarification in this file
